pricing_framing: Add market context above the price options: "NYC escape rooms typically range $35–$44 per person (validated market data from Mission Escape Games and Escape the Room NYC). This Groupon offers online booking convenience for 6 different themed rooms at one Manhattan location, with flexible weekday and weekend scheduling. The merchant's direct site shows $40/person for groups of 4-12. Position the value around: (1) guaranteed Groupon booking with 3-day refund, (2) choice of 6 themes in one location vs. traveling to multiple venues, (3) weekend availability included. Do NOT claim this is the lowest price — emphasize convenience, variety, and flexible scheduling instead."
executive_summary: The page scores 5.7/10, but the core problem is pricing: at $49.49/person, this deal is 12-41% ABOVE the validated NYC market range of $35–$44/person and appears more expensive than the merchant's own $40/person direct booking (MODERATE confidence, 50% SKU match). Copy optimization cannot fix a structural pricing disadvantage. The top 3 fixes are: (1) add honest value framing emphasizing convenience over savings (value_comm: 4/10 — no original price or context shown), (2) add missing session duration (completeness: 6/10 — critical gap for planning), and (3) remove stale pandemic-era content flagged by AI. These changes may reduce hesitation and abandonment by 8–12%, but the deal will remain uncompetitive on price alone.

image_recommendations.image_type: Action shots of diverse groups actively playing — people examining clues, pointing at puzzles, excited expressions during gameplay
image_recommendations.conversion_reason: Escape rooms sell an experience, not a product. Showing real people engaged and excited helps buyers visualize themselves in the scenario and reduces uncertainty about what they're actually purchasing. The current page likely has generic room photos but lacks human emotional connection.

image_recommendations.image_type: Individual photos of all 6 room themes with distinct visual settings — murder mystery office, bank vault, quarantine lab, etc.
image_recommendations.conversion_reason: With 6 different rooms offered, buyers need to see what makes each unique to make their choice confidently. Visual differentiation reduces decision paralysis and helps groups agree on which room to book, reducing abandonment at the booking step.

image_recommendations.image_type: Close-up shots of actual puzzles, locks, props, or clue elements from the rooms (without spoiling solutions)
image_recommendations.conversion_reason: Showing tangible puzzle elements builds anticipation and helps first-time escape room customers understand what 'solving puzzles' actually means. This bridges the knowledge gap for the uninitiated and increases perceived value of the 60-minute experience.

image_recommendations.image_type: Exterior storefront or building entrance photo clearly showing the Manhattan location and floor signage (5th/6th floor mentioned in audit)
image_recommendations.conversion_reason: Content gap: no full street address shown. A recognizable exterior photo helps NYC customers assess exact location convenience and builds confidence they can find the venue. Critical for a multi-floor location that may be harder to locate.

image_recommendations.image_type: Photo of game master greeting or briefing a group in the lobby/waiting area
image_recommendations.conversion_reason: Adds human element and trust signal. Shows there's professional staff facilitating the experience, which matters for a merchant with only 23 Groupon reviews and no independent Yelp/Google reviews found in research.
